stem: A 9-year-old girl is booked for a minor painful skin procedure in a paediatric surgical clinic and topical anaesthetic cream is planned; when should it be applied?

options.text: After the procedure if pain persists

explanation: Topical anaesthetic cream should be applied 1 hour before the procedure to allow adequate effect.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because immediate application does not allow enough time for topical anaesthetic to work.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because 15 minutes is shorter than the recommended pre-procedure timing.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because 30 minutes is not the timing specified for effective pre-procedure use.
optionExplanations.D: Correct because topical anaesthetic cream is applied 1 hour before the procedure to provide adequate anaesthesia.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because topical anaesthetic is used before the procedure, not as a post-procedure treatment for persistent pain.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
